summary: A scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Tenzin Namdak studied under sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan, Lobpön Tsultrim Gyaltsen, and at Menri Monastery (1950–1953). In 1986, he founded Triten Norbutse Monastery.

Specializing in Tibetology, religious studies, and philosophy, he earned his Geshe degree at Menri Monastery's Dialectic School. He served as its director (~1986–1989), held posts at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and founded Ligmincha International.

A scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Ter Ellingson studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1979). He held a post at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

Active in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology, Bartholomew earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles. She held posts at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco, including Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art (attested 2001–2003).
Tertön Sogyal studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. During his career, he taught the 13th Dalai Lama.

A religious studies and philosophy scholar, Ishizu studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). His posts included president of Tohoku University (1963–1966), president of Miyagi University of Education (1965), and professorships at Keio and Komazawa universities (1966).

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Bartholomeusz studied at the University of Florida, Florida State University, and the University of Virginia (PhD 1991). She taught religious studies at Indiana University Indianapolis (~1991–2001) and Florida State University (1993).
A scholar in history and archaeology, Tessa Verney Wheeler completed her early education at Addey and Stanhope School (1905–1911) and later studied at University College London from 1911 to 1914.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Tetsuei Sato studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He held professorships at Taisho University and Gifu Keizai University (~1968–1974), and served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1968–1982).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tetsuhiko Shibata studied at Taisho University under teachers Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

A philosopher and religious studies scholar, Inoue studied at Tokyo Kaisei School, University of Tokyo, Heidelberg, and Leipzig. He was professor and dean at the University of Tokyo (1890, 1898) and served as president of Daito Bunka University (1925).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Otani studied at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He served as professor and president of Komazawa University (2002–2006) and later held presidencies at Tsuru University (2013–2016) and Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

A scholar in sinology, history and archaeology, and religious studies, Tetsuro Noguchi held academic posts at Yokohama National University (~1967–1977), the University of Tsukuba (~1977–1996), and J. F. Oberlin University (~1996–2003).

Watsuji worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, and under Martin Heidegger, he served as professor of ethics at Kyoto University (1931–1934) and held the ethics chair at Tokyo (1934–1949).

A philosophy scholar, Tetsuzo Tanikawa studied at Kyoto University's Faculty of Letters (~1919–1922). He later held academic posts at Doshisha University (~1928–1931) and served as a professor at Hosei University (~1938–1968).
Teun Goudriaan was a scholar in indology and religious studies who held a post at Utrecht University (attested 1989), where he later served as Professor Emeritus (attested 2000).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Thanissaro Bhikkhu studied at Oberlin College (~1967–1971) and trained under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko (~1972–1986). He co-founded Metta Forest Monastery, serving as its abbot beginning in 1993.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Thegchog Dorje studied under Pema Nyinje Wangpo and Kunzik Chokyi Nangwa. As a teacher, his prominent students included Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Chokgyur Lingpa.

An indologist and linguist, Aufrecht studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1843–1847). He served as Privatdozent in Berlin (1850), held a post at the Bodleian Library (1852), and became professor at Edinburgh (1861–1875) and Bonn (1875–1889).

An indologist and linguist, Theodor Benfey studied at the University of Göttingen and the University of Munich. He spent his career at the University of Göttingen, serving as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius professor (1862–1881).
